atoms.text: Hamsters are a small nocturnal rodent. They love to exercise and make a great pet for families. Did you know that hamsters were first found in the desert in Syria? Due to hamsters being used to such warm weather in the desert, it is important to keep their cages in a warm and cosy space in your home. Since they are used to the desert, they also don’t wash with water but with sand instead so make sure you don’t bathe them as it is harmful to them.

atoms.text: Hamsters are also extremely active animals and love to run around, especially at night since they are mostly nocturnal animals. Although they are mostly active at night, they do also come out in the day sometimes. Hamsters are crepuscular animals. Did you know that, even though they may be tiny, hamsters can run up to 8 miles when they exercise? It’s therefore very important for hamsters to have a wheel in their cage or an exercise ball in which they can run around the house in.

atoms.text: Hamsters are omnivores which means that they will eat plant-based as well as meat-based foods. Hamsters often love to eat snacks such as fruit and nuts but also love mealworms which can easily be found in shops. A very famous trait of hamsters is the way they hoard food in the pouches in their cheeks to eat later. They do this especially in winter when they are about to hibernate so that they can store supplies for when it’s cold.

atoms.text: In the wild, hamsters dig underground tunnels and live in 'burrows' away from predators and the cold. These burrows can be extremely deep underground, sometimes 5 to 6 feet deep! When we keep hamsters in our homes, it is therefore important to create an environment in which they feel at home, which is why we put down wood shavings. These wood shavings allow hamsters to burrow just as they would in the wild.
